long_biography.plain_text:
After a decade in Singapore, Mahoney could draw specialist Thai teak from his own mill for a technically demanding British restoration. Work planned in the 1970s would combine structural steel, traditional rigging and auxiliary engines. A Southampton yard would handle the project to a recognised marine standard.

Mahoney approached the undertaking as an international operation. He anticipated extended cruising, recruited a large crew and linked suppliers and sailors across Southeast Asia, Australia and the United Kingdom. The project therefore required more than personal enthusiasm: it joined control of materials with logistics, technical coordination and preservation. That combination offers the clearest surviving view of how he applied his industrial resources beyond ordinary commercial work.
